title: Ai is making me question own capabilities
author: Affectionate_Fact854
selftext:
So for context 

I have been building angular web apps prior to using godot 

I even built my own tap titans without ai in angular to test it's capabilities while I started my coding journey 4 years ago 

  
I moved to godot , spent 3 months of tutorial hell and documentation hell

Then started with making games like pinball and pong 

  
Worked on a arpg in godot for about 1 year , with no ai , just learning how to use the engine and how to optimize draw calls and understand what i like 

  
Then i started another project when i shelfed the first one because of feature creep

  
This one i did 80% myself 

And started slowly using ai assisted debugging which dramatically reduced the time i would get stuck or bounty hunt typos

Eventually had it help me with complex tasks like setting up uniform spacial grids with snapshots , so that projectiles and enemy bodies could query this instead of using the godot physics engine 



Im proud of that project , cant believe how far i have gotten over the course of repetitive learning on a almost daily basis

  
I now started testing ai capabilities with agentic work flow 

  
Set up full structure orchestrator,quality assurer and a workforce underneath

Clear instructions and phased goals 

  
The outcome of the code base this has provided for a test project looks so clean...

It looks 2x cleaner then what im even capable of producing 

  
At this point i feel the only thing im able to bring to the table for it is experience of telling it what optimization strategies it has to implement from the start, telling it what autoloader managers must exist and what else must be managers within the stage scene only....

Im afraid that will eventually also be worthless to ai as it improves...

comments.author: tastychaii
comments.body:
“Set up full structure orchestrator,quality assurer and a workforce underneath”  
How did you set this up if you don’t mind me asking? Are there any guides that walkthrough this as well?

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Honestly no, I just tested 1 method last week where I'm the orchestrator (do not recommend that at all) 

Decided this week let's try something else 

I went with opencode windows app 

You basically set up .MD files 
That the ai reads prior to anything 

The boot.md would contain. MD files like 

Gamedesign. Development_phase.  Workspace. Research. Index.  Handover.   Rules.   

You would let it set up a order of operations 

Have a few agents on standby , each having its dedicated role (skillset) 

Let the coders code, hand over report to the orchestrator that knows everything , he will instruct a quality assurer to inspect and test new features with a rule (don't trust coders test reports) 

After it would hand back to orchestrator with a pass 

Orchestrator will go down the phase of development form 

And decide what agents to now put to work if there's still open tasks.
If no tasks open o
rchestrator does a final hand over , and waits for your testing and input 

If you tested , and are happy it closes the phase , and you just start a new conversation and hand the new orchestrator the boot.md 

And it will automatically start on the next phase of implementation 



There's probably even better methods that would blow my mind but this so far is out classing my manual workflow...

comments.author: seahorse-emoji
comments.body:
I think of the advent of AI in a similar vein to Auto mode on cameras.

Auto mode allows a lot more people to take passable, even interesting photos. BUT, you still hire a photographer to shoot your wedding.

Certainly, more accessible cameras changed everyone's relationship to cameras and photography, but taking good photos is still a skill.

Bringing the analogy back, in ye olden days (2 years ago). Game devs had to operate in Ansel Adams mode, now , we are starting to figure out what happens when you don't need to carry a massive camera up inaccessible hiking paths to take beautiful photos of mountains.
